techList.name: React
techList.desc: Massive ecosystem and hiring pool. The default choice for most product teams.

techList.name: Angular
techList.desc: Batteries-included, TypeScript-first. Best for large enterprise teams needing structure.

techList.name: Vue
techList.desc: Gentle learning curve, flexible. Great for small-to-mid teams shipping fast.

techList.name: Svelte
techList.desc: Compiles away at build time, smallest bundles. Best when performance is the top priority.

techList.name: Next.js
techList.desc: React plus routing, SSR, and static generation built in. Best for SEO-heavy or full-stack apps.

techList.name: Java / Spring
techList.desc: Verbose but rock-solid. Huge hiring pool. Runs untouched for years.

techList.name: C# / .NET
techList.desc: Same strengths as Java, nicer tooling, fully cross-platform now.

techList.name: Python / Django
techList.desc: Fastest to a working system. Free admin screens. Weaker on huge domains.

techList.name: Node / TypeScript
techList.desc: One language front to back. Fast hiring, but watch dependency churn.

techList.name: Go
techList.desc: Single binary, trivial to deploy. Best for infrastructure-heavy systems.

techList.name: PHP / Laravel
techList.desc: Cheapest hosting, huge SME footprint. Do not sneer, it ships.

title:
How the Choice
Is Really Made

techList.name: Who can we hire, years from now?
techList.desc: The system outlives its author. Hiring pool beats elegance.

techList.name: What does the team already know?
techList.desc: A second system in a familiar language beats a first in a better one.

techList.name: Does the ecosystem fit the domain?
techList.desc: Ready-made libraries for your exact problem remove weeks of work.

techList.name: How hard is it to operate?
techList.desc: Fewer moving parts, fewer 9 p.m. phone calls.

callout.label: The reason that should not decide it
callout.body:
"Which one is fastest?" At real-world
        scale, every modern option on the list is fast enough.

techList.name: PostgreSQL
techList.desc: Relational. Open-source, built for correctness. The default choice for structured, must-be-right data.

techList.name: MySQL
techList.desc: Relational. The most widely hosted open-source database, huge SME footprint.

techList.name: MS SQL Server
techList.desc: Relational. Microsoft's enterprise database, deep .NET integration.

techList.name: Oracle
techList.desc: Relational. The backbone of large legacy enterprises — banking, telecom, government.

techList.name: MongoDB
techList.desc: Document. Flexible JSON-like records instead of rigid tables — good when the shape of data varies.

techList.name: Redis
techList.desc: Key-Value. Near-instant lookups by a key you know. Caching only, never your main record.

callout.label: Three shapes, three jobs
callout.body: Relational (structured tables), Document (flexible JSON), Key-Value (instant lookups). Pick based on how you'll query the data, not habit.

techList.name: Monolith
techList.desc: Everything in one program. Simple to build, but one bug can affect every store at once.

techList.name: Modular Monolith
techList.desc: Still one program, but cleanly divided inside — like labelled drawers in one cabinet.

techList.name: Microservices
techList.desc: Many small, independent programs. Flexible, but harder to keep in sync with each other.

techList.name: Hybrid (what we build)
techList.desc: One central system, plus a lightweight copy in every store, so billing never fully stops.

techList.name: Unit Test
techList.desc: Checks one small piece of code by itself — like "does the tax calculator give the right number?"

techList.name: Integration Test
techList.desc: Checks that your code and the real database actually work together, not just in isolation.

techList.name: Concurrency Test
techList.desc: Makes sure two people billing the same last item at the same moment can't both succeed.

callout.label: Live on stage
callout.body: a real pull request, from branch to merge, with this exact test suite running against it.

techList.name: CI/CD Pipeline
techList.desc: An automatic checklist that tests and ships every code change, so nothing broken reaches a real store.

techList.name: Monitoring
techList.desc: A dashboard that watches whether the system is healthy — a checkup that runs every second, not once a year.

techList.name: Rollback
techList.desc: If a release breaks something, the system can automatically bring back the last version that worked.

callout.label: Live on stage
callout.body: a real deploy, a live dashboard, and a deliberately broken release to show the rollback actually firing.

techList.desc: Drafting requirements, comparing tech options, writing boilerplate, generating tests.

techList.name: What did not move
techList.desc: Deciding what to build, owning an outage, and knowing when to say no.

techList.desc: Learn to read code critically, not just write it. That's the scarce skill now.
